title: TCP/IP stack, protocols and DNS
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: Choose the model answer: Which device typically forwards packets between different IP networks?
Choose the model answer: What does an edge represent in a network graph?
Choose the model answer: How many bits make one byte?
Choose the model answer: A sender and receiver are on different networks. Can a switch alone normally route IP packets between them?
questions.answer: No. A router (or routing-capable layer-3 switch) is needed to route between IP networks.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: application layer — Protocols offering services to applications, including DNS and HTTP.
transport layer — End-to-end transport protocols such as TCP and UDP.
internet layer — Network addressing and forwarding using IP.
link layer — Local transfer of frames over media such as Ethernet or Wi-Fi.
DNS — Domain Name System; supports name-to-address resolution.

blocks.title: Start with a hostname
blocks.text: The browser uses DNS (an application-layer protocol) to resolve school.example to an IP address. A cached result may avoid further queries.

blocks.title: Understand four layers
blocks.text: Application supports services such as HTTP(S), DNS and SMTP; transport includes TCP and UDP; internet uses IP; link transfers frames on the local connection.

blocks.title: Build an HTTPS connection
blocks.text: A browser normally establishes TCP to port 443, negotiates TLS, then exchanges encrypted HTTP requests and responses. DNS lookup happens first if the IP is unknown.

blocks.title: Worked example · Name resolution
blocks.text: The resolver returns the IP address for library.example (or uses a cached answer).

blocks.title: Worked example · Transport connection
blocks.text: TCP establishes a connection to the server, typically destination port 443.

blocks.title: Identify the application
blocks.text: SMTP is an application-layer protocol for transferring outgoing email.

blocks.title: Identify the other layers
blocks.text: TCP provides reliable transport for SMTP; IP handles inter-network addressing and routing; link delivers frames on each local link.
